units.Nehemiah 5:1: A great outcry arose from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.

units.Nehemiah 5:9: I said, “What you are doing is not good. Not so! In the fear of our God you shall depart from the reproach of the nations, our enemies.

units.Hebrews 6:13: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater by whom to swear, He swore by Himself,
units.Hebrews 6:14: saying, “Surely, blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
units.Hebrews 6:15: And so, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
units.Hebrews 6:16: For people swear by one greater, and among them an oath for confirmation ends every dispute.
units.Hebrews 6:17: In this, God, wishing to show more fully to the heirs of the promise the unchanging nature of His purpose, intervened with an oath,
units.Hebrews 6:18: so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast the hope set before us.
units.Amos 9:1: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar. He said, “Strike the atonement cover, and the foregates will shake; cut through the heads of all. I will kill their survivors with a sword. No one fleeing from among them will escape, and no one seeking safety will be saved.
units.Amos 9:2: If they burrow into Hades, My hand will pull them up from there; if they climb to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
units.Amos 9:3: If they hide on Carmel’s summit, I will search them out and take them from there. If they plunge from My eyes into the sea’s depths, I will command the dragon there, and it will bite them.
units.Amos 9:4: If they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there, and it will kill them. I will fix My eyes upon them for evils and not for good things.”
units.Deuteronomy 18:15: The Lord your God shall raise up unto you a prophet from among your brethren, like unto me; you shall hearken unto him,
units.Deuteronomy 18:16: according to all that you asked of the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, saying: We will no more hear the voice of the Lord our God, neither will we see this great fire any more, lest we die.
units.Deuteronomy 18:17: And the Lord said unto me: All that they have spoken is right.
units.Deuteronomy 18:18: I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brethren, like unto you, and will put My word in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I command him.
units.Deuteronomy 18:19: And the man who will not hearken unto whatsoever the prophet shall speak in My name, I will exact retribution from him.
units.Deuteronomy 18:20: But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
units.Deuteronomy 18:21: And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken?
units.Deuteronomy 18:22: Whatsoever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come to pass, nor is fulfilled, that is the word which the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken in ungodliness; you shall not spare him.
units.Psalms 6:1: For the end, among hymns, concerning the eighth. A psalm of David.
units.Psalms 6:2: Lord, do not rebuke me in Thy fury, nor discipline me in Thine anger.
units.Psalms 6:3: Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord, for my bones were troubled,
units.Psalms 6:4: and my soul was greatly troubled. And Thou, Lord—how long?
units.Psalms 6:5: Return, Lord; rescue my soul. Save me for the sake of Thy mercy.
units.Psalms 6:6: For in death there is no one who remembers Thee; and in Hades, who will give Thee thanks?
units.Psalms 6:7: I grew weary with my groaning; every night I will bathe my bed, with my tears I will wet my resting place.
units.Psalms 6:8: My eye was troubled from anger; I grew old among all my enemies.
units.Psalms 6:9: Stand away from me, all who work lawlessness, for the Lord heard the voice of my weeping.
units.Psalms 6:10: The Lord heard my petition; the Lord accepted my prayer.

units.Psalms 130:3: Let Israel hope in the Lord, from now and for ever.

units.Ezekiel 12:14: All those around him, his helpers and all who support him, I will scatter to every wind; I will draw a sword after them.

units.1 Kings 7:13: Twelve cattle were beneath the Sea: three facing north, three facing the sea, three facing south, and three facing east. All their hindquarters faced the house, and the Sea was above them.
units.1 Kings 7:14: He made ten bronze stands. Each stand was five cubits long, four cubits wide, and six cubits high.
units.1 Kings 7:15: This was the construction of the stands: they had enclosed panels, and enclosed panels between the projecting parts.
units.1 Kings 7:16: On their enclosed panels between the projecting parts were lions, cattle, and cherubim, and likewise on the projecting parts. Above and below the lions and cattle were spaces, in descending work.
units.1 Kings 7:17: Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze attachments; their four parts had shoulders beneath the basins.
units.1 Kings 7:18: The wheels’ arms were in the stand, and the height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
units.1 Kings 7:19: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their arms, backs, and assembled work were all cast.
units.1 Kings 7:20: Each stand had four shoulders at its four corners; its shoulders were of one piece with the stand.
units.1 Kings 7:21: At the top of the stand was a round part half a cubit in size, all around at its top, with the beginnings of its arms and its enclosed panels; it opened onto the beginnings of its arms.
units.1 Kings 7:22: Its enclosed panels had cherubim, lions, and palm trees standing, each adjoining the next toward its front, inside and all around.
units.1 Kings 7:23: According to this pattern he made all ten stands, with one arrangement and one measure for all.
units.1 Kings 7:24: He made ten bronze basin vessels; each basin vessel held forty choes by measure. There was one basin vessel on each of the ten stands.
units.1 Kings 7:25: He placed the ten stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left. The Sea was on the right side of the house, eastward toward the southern slope.
units.1 Kings 7:26: Hiram made the cauldrons, braziers, and bowls. Hiram finished all the works that he did for King Solomon in the Lord’s house:
units.1 Kings 7:27: two pillars, the two twisted ornaments of the pillars on top of the pillars, and the two nets covering both twisted ornaments of the carvings on the pillars;
units.1 Kings 7:28: four hundred pomegranates for both nets, two rows of pomegranates for each net, covering both twisted ornaments on both pillars;
units.1 Kings 7:40: He paneled the house above, over the sides of the pillars. The number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen to a row.
units.1 Kings 7:41: There were three beams, and space above space in three tiers.
units.1 Kings 7:42: All the doorways and spaces were square and fitted with beams, with doorway facing door in three tiers.
units.1 Kings 7:43: The porch of the pillars was fifty cubits long and thirty wide, joined together, with a porch in front of them, and pillars and a thick structure in front of it for the porches.
units.1 Kings 7:44: There was the porch of the thrones, where he would judge, the porch of the judgment hall.
units.1 Kings 7:45: He had a house where he would live, with one court opening around these, according to this workmanship; and a house for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Solomon had married, corresponding to this porch.
units.1 Kings 7:46: All these were of costly stones, carved at intervals inside, from the foundation to the cornices, and outside as far as the great court,
units.1 Kings 7:47: which was founded on costly, great stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits,

units.2 Chronicles 3:17: He erected the pillars before the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He named the one on the right Establishment and the one on the left Strength.
units.1 Kings 7:1: King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre,
units.1 Kings 7:2: a widow’s son, and he was from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a Tyrian man, a bronze craftsman, filled with skill, understanding, and knowledge for doing every work in bronze. He was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.
units.1 Kings 7:3: He cast the two pillars for the house’s porch. The pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a circumference of fourteen cubits encircled it. The pillar’s thickness was four fingerbreadths, with hollow spaces; and the second pillar was the same.
units.1 Kings 7:4: He made two capitals to place on top of the pillars, of cast bronze. One capital was five cubits high, and the second capital was five cubits high.
units.1 Kings 7:5: He made two nets to cover the pillars’ capital: one net for one capital and one net for the second capital.
units.1 Kings 7:6: There was hanging work: two rows of bronze pomegranates interwoven as a net, hanging work, row upon row. He did likewise for the second capital.
units.1 Kings 7:7: He set up the pillars of the temple’s porch. He set up one pillar and called it Iachoum; he set up the second pillar and called it Boaz.
units.1 Kings 7:8: On top of the pillars was lily-work corresponding to the porch, four cubits.
units.1 Kings 7:9: There was a beam over both pillars, and above the sides the beam formed a capital in its thickness.
units.1 Kings 7:10: He made the Sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, round all around and five cubits high; thirty-three cubits in all encircled it.
units.1 Kings 7:11: Supports encircled it beneath its brim all around, ten to a cubit, holding up the Sea all around.
units.1 Kings 7:12: Its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily shoot, and its thickness was a palm.

units.Jeremiah 41:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his whole army, and all the land under his rule were fighting Jerusalem and all Judah’s cities:
units.Jeremiah 41:2: Thus said the Lord: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, Thus said the Lord: This city will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king. He will seize it and burn it with fire.
units.Jeremiah 41:3: You will certainly not be saved from his hand. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. Your eyes will see his eyes, and his mouth will speak with your mouth. You will enter Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 41:4: But hear the Lord’s word, Zedekiah king of Judah. Thus says the Lord:
units.Jeremiah 41:5: You will die in peace. As they wept for your fathers who reigned before you, they will weep for you and lament you, O lord! For I have spoken the word, said the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 41:6: Jeremiah spoke all these words to King Zedekiah in Jerusalem,
units.Jeremiah 41:7: while Babylon’s king’s force fought Jerusalem and Judah’s cities, Lachish and Azekah; these were the fortified cities left among Judah’s cities.
units.Jeremiah 41:8: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah concluded a covenant with the people to proclaim release:
units.Jeremiah 41:9: each was to send his Hebrew male slave and his Hebrew female slave away free, so that a man from Judah would not be enslaved.
units.Jeremiah 41:10: All the magnates and all the people who had entered the covenant to send away their male and female slaves turned back,
units.Jeremiah 41:11: and thrust them into the position of male and female slaves.
units.Jeremiah 41:12: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
units.Jeremiah 41:13: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: I established a covenant with your fathers on the day I rescued them from Egypt, from the house of slavery, saying:
units.Jeremiah 41:14: When six years are complete, you must send away your Hebrew brother who is sold to you. He will work for you six years, and you must send him away free. But they did not obey Me or incline their ears.
units.Jeremiah 41:15: Today they turned to do what was right before My eyes, each proclaiming his neighbor’s release. They concluded a covenant before Me in the house over which My name is invoked.
units.Jeremiah 41:16: Then you reversed yourselves and profaned My name by bringing back your male and female slaves, whom you had sent away free in their own persons, to be your slaves.
units.Jeremiah 41:17: Therefore thus said the Lord: You did not obey Me by proclaiming release, each to his neighbor. So I proclaim release for you to sword, death, and famine! I will give you over to scattering among all the earth’s kingdoms.
units.Jeremiah 41:18: I will hand over the men who passed beyond My covenant, who did not uphold My covenant which they made before Me—the calf they made, to work for it—
units.Jeremiah 41:19: Judah’s rulers, the powerful men, the priests, and the people.
units.Jeremiah 41:20: I will hand them over to their enemies, and their carcasses will become food for the birds of heaven and the wild beasts of the earth.
units.Jeremiah 41:21: I will hand Zedekiah king of Judea and their rulers over to their enemies. And the force of Babylon’s king is for those running away from them.
units.Jeremiah 41:22: I am giving orders, says the Lord, and will bring them back to this land. They will fight against it, take it, and burn it with fire, along with Judah’s cities; I will make them deserted of inhabitants.
units.Jeremiah 42:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim king of Judah:
units.Jeremiah 42:2: Go to the house of the Rechabites. Bring them into the Lord’s house, into one of the courts, and give them wine to drink.
units.Jeremiah 42:3: I brought out Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, his brothers, his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites.
units.Jeremiah 42:4: I brought them into the Lord’s house, into the chamber of the sons of Hananiah son of Gedaliah, the man of God. It is near the house of the rulers above the house of Maaseiah son of Shallum, who guards the court.
units.Jeremiah 42:5: I set before them an earthenware jar of wine and cups, and said, Drink wine.
units.Jeremiah 42:6: They said, We certainly will not drink wine, because Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us: Neither you nor your sons must ever drink wine.
units.Jeremiah 42:7: You must not build a house or sow seed, and you must not have a vineyard. You must live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the land where you spend your time.
units.Jeremiah 42:8: We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab our father by not drinking wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters,
units.Jeremiah 42:9: and by not building houses to live there. We have had no vineyard, field, or sown crop.
units.Jeremiah 42:10: We lived in tents, obeying and doing everything Jonadab our father commanded us.
units.Jeremiah 42:11: When Nebuchadnezzar invaded the land, we said, Come in, let us enter Jerusalem to escape the Chaldean force and the Assyrian force. So we were living there.
units.Jeremiah 42:12: The Lord’s word came to me:
units.Jeremiah 42:13: Thus says the Lord: Go and say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants, Will you really not accept discipline and hear My words?
units.Jeremiah 42:14: The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld the word he commanded his children, not to drink wine, and they drank none. Yet I spoke to you from early morning and kept speaking, and you did not listen.
units.Jeremiah 42:15: I sent you My servants the prophets, saying, Each of you, turn from his evil way and improve your practices. Do not follow other gods to serve them, and you will live on the land I gave you and your fathers. But you did not incline your ears or listen.
units.Jeremiah 42:16: The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld their father’s command, but this people did not obey Me.
units.Jeremiah 42:17: Therefore thus said the Lord: I am bringing upon Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants all the calamities I pronounced against them.
units.Jeremiah 42:18: Therefore thus said the Lord: Because the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab obeyed their father’s command, doing as their father commanded them,
units.Jeremiah 42:19: there will certainly never fail a man from the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab standing before Me all the earth’s days.
units.Jeremiah 43:1: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the Lord’s word came to me:
units.Jeremiah 43:2: Take a writing roll and write on it all the words I have delivered to you as oracles concerning Jerusalem, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah until today.
units.Jeremiah 43:3: Perhaps Judah’s house will hear all the calamities I intend to bring upon them, so that they turn from their evil way and I may be merciful toward their injustices and sins.
units.Jeremiah 43:4: Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and he wrote on a writing roll, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the Lord’s words which He had delivered to him as oracles.
units.Jeremiah 43:5: Jeremiah instructed Baruch, I am under guard and cannot enter the Lord’s house.
units.Jeremiah 43:6: Read from this roll in the people’s hearing at the Lord’s house on a fast day, and read it to all Judah’s people coming from their city.
units.Jeremiah 43:7: Perhaps their appeal for mercy will fall before the Lord, and they will turn from their evil way, for great are the Lord’s wrath and anger which He has pronounced against this people.
units.Jeremiah 43:8: Baruch did everything Jeremiah instructed him, reading the Lord’s words from the document in the Lord’s house.
units.Jeremiah 43:9: In King Jehoiakim’s eighth year, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and Judah’s house assembled for a fast before the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 43:10: Baruch read Jeremiah’s words from the document in the Lord’s house, in the house of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the Lord’s house, in all the people’s hearing.
units.Jeremiah 43:11: Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the Lord’s words from the document.
units.Jeremiah 43:12: He went down to the king’s house, to the scribe’s house. All the rulers were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shelemiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the rulers.
units.Jeremiah 43:13: Micaiah reported to them all the words he had heard when Baruch read in the people’s hearing.
units.Jeremiah 43:14: All the rulers sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch son of Neriah, saying, Take in your hand the roll from which you are reading to the people, and come. Baruch took the roll and went down to them.
units.Jeremiah 43:15: They said to him, Read it again to us. Baruch read it.
units.Jeremiah 43:16: When they heard all the words, they consulted one another and said, Let us certainly report all these words to the king.
units.Jeremiah 43:17: They asked Baruch, Where did all these words you wrote come from?
units.Jeremiah 43:18: Baruch said, Jeremiah reported all these words to me from his mouth, and I wrote them in a document.
units.Jeremiah 43:19: They said to Baruch, Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Let no one know where you are.
units.Jeremiah 43:20: They entered the court to see the king, leaving the roll for safekeeping in Elishama’s house, and reported all the words to the king.
units.Jeremiah 43:21: The king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll. He took it from Elishama’s house, and Jehudi read it to the king and all the rulers standing around him.
units.Jeremiah 43:22: The king was sitting in a winter house, with a fire brazier before him.
units.Jeremiah 43:23: When Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut them off with the scribe’s knife and threw them into the fire on the brazier, until the whole roll was consumed in the brazier’s fire.
units.Jeremiah 43:24: Neither the king nor his servants who heard all these words sought anything or tore their garments.
units.Jeremiah 43:25: Elnathan, Gedaliah, and Gemariah advised the king not to burn the roll.
units.Jeremiah 43:26: The king ordered Jerahmeel the king’s son and Seraiah son of Azriel to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah. But they were hidden.
units.Jeremiah 43:27: After the king burned the roll—all the words Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth—the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
units.Jeremiah 43:28: Take another roll again and write all the words that were on the roll which King Jehoiakim burned.
units.Jeremiah 43:29: Say, Thus said the Lord: You burned this roll, saying, Why did you write in it that Babylon’s king will certainly enter and destroy this land, and people and animals will cease from it?
units.Jeremiah 43:30: Therefore thus said the Lord concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one sitting on David’s throne. His carcass will be thrown out in the day’s heat and the night’s frost.
units.Jeremiah 43:31: I will visit him, his family, and his servants, and bring upon them, Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and Judah’s land all the calamities I pronounced to them, but they did not listen.
units.Jeremiah 43:32: Baruch took another roll and wrote on it, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the words of the document Jehoiakim burned. Still more words like these were added to it.
units.Jeremiah 44:1: Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Jehoiakim; Nebuchadnezzar had made him king over Judah.
units.Jeremiah 44:2: Neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land obeyed the Lord’s words, which He spoke through Jeremiah.
units.Jeremiah 44:3: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah, saying, Please pray for us to the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 44:4: Jeremiah came and passed through the midst of the city; they had not put him in prison.
units.Jeremiah 44:5: Pharaoh’s force came out of Egypt. The Chaldeans heard the report about them and withdrew from Jerusalem.
units.Jeremiah 44:6: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
units.Jeremiah 44:7: Thus said the Lord: Tell Judah’s king, who sent to you to seek Me, Pharaoh’s force, which came out to help you, will return to Egypt’s land.
units.Jeremiah 44:8: The Chaldeans themselves will return, fight this city, seize it, and burn it with fire.
units.Jeremiah 44:9: For thus said the Lord: Do not suppose within yourselves, The Chaldeans will flee and leave us. They certainly will not leave.
units.Jeremiah 44:10: Even if you struck the whole Chaldean force fighting you and some were left pierced through, each in his place, these would rise and burn this city with fire.
units.Jeremiah 44:11: When the Chaldean force withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh’s force,
units.Jeremiah 44:12: Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to Benjamin’s land, to buy from there among the people.
units.Jeremiah 44:13: At Benjamin’s Gate there was a man with whom he lodged, Sarouiah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah. He arrested Jeremiah, saying, You are fleeing to the Chaldeans!
units.Jeremiah 44:14: He said, A lie! I am not fleeing to the Chaldeans. But Sarouiah would not listen to him; he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the rulers.
units.Jeremiah 44:15: The rulers were embittered against Jeremiah. They struck him and sent him into the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had made into a prison house.
units.Jeremiah 44:16: Jeremiah entered the pit-house and the chereth and stayed there many days.
units.Jeremiah 44:17: Zedekiah sent and summoned him. The king secretly asked him whether there was a word from the Lord. He said, There is. You will be handed over to Babylon’s king.
units.Jeremiah 44:18: Jeremiah said to the king, How have I wronged you, your servants, or this people, that you are putting me in prison?
units.Jeremiah 44:19: Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, Babylon’s king certainly will not come against this land?
units.Jeremiah 44:20: Now, lord king, let my appeal for mercy fall before you. Why send me back to Jonathan the scribe’s house—and will I not die there?
units.Jeremiah 44:21: The king gave orders, and they put him into the prison house, giving him one loaf a day from outside where they bake, until the city’s loaves ran out. Jeremiah remained in the prison court.
units.Jeremiah 45:1: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jehucal son of Shelemiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to the people:
units.Jeremiah 45:2: Thus said the Lord: Whoever remains in this city will die by sword and famine. Whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; his life will be his gain, and he will live.
units.Jeremiah 45:3: For thus said the Lord: This city will certainly be handed over to the force of Babylon’s king, and he will seize it.
units.Jeremiah 45:4: They said to the king, Let that man be killed! By speaking these words to them he weakens the hands of the fighters left in the city and of all the people. This man delivers oracles of evil to this people, not peace.
units.Jeremiah 45:5: The king said, He is in your hands—for the king was unable to oppose them.
units.Jeremiah 45:6: They threw him into the pit of Malchiah the king’s son in the prison court and lowered him into the pit. There was no water in it, only mire, and he was in the mire.
units.Jeremiah 45:7: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the pit. The king was at Benjamin’s Gate.
units.Jeremiah 45:8: He went out to him, spoke to the king, and said:
units.Jeremiah 45:9: You have acted wickedly in what you did, killing this man through hunger, for there are no more loaves in the city.
units.Jeremiah 45:10: The king instructed Ebed-melech, Take thirty men from here under your command and bring him up from the pit so that he does not die.
units.Jeremiah 45:11: Ebed-melech took the men and entered the king’s underground house. He took old rags and old ropes from there and threw them down to Jeremiah in the pit.
units.Jeremiah 45:12: He said, Put these beneath the ropes. Jeremiah did so.
units.Jeremiah 45:13: They pulled him with the ropes and brought him up from the pit. Jeremiah remained in the prison court.
units.Jeremiah 45:14: The king sent and summoned him to himself, to the aselisi house in the Lord’s house. The king said to him, I will ask you something. Please hide no word from me.
units.Jeremiah 45:15: Jeremiah said to the king, If I tell you, will you not certainly put me to death? And if I advise you, you certainly will not listen to me.
units.Jeremiah 45:16: The king swore to him, As the Lord lives, who made this life for us, I will not kill you or hand you over to these men.
units.Jeremiah 45:17: Jeremiah said to him, Thus said the Lord: If you go out to Babylon’s king’s commanders, your life will be spared and this city will certainly not be burned with fire. You and your household will live.
units.Jeremiah 45:18: But if you do not go out, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans and they will burn it with fire. You certainly will not be saved.
units.Jeremiah 45:19: The king said to Jeremiah, I am concerned about the Judeans who have fled to the Chaldeans, lest they hand me over to them and mock me.
units.Jeremiah 45:20: Jeremiah said, They certainly will not hand you over. Hear the Lord’s word which I speak to you, and it will be better for you; your life will be spared.
units.Jeremiah 45:21: But if you are unwilling to go out, this is the word the Lord showed me:
units.Jeremiah 45:22: All the women left in Judah’s king’s house were being brought out to Babylon’s king’s rulers. They said, Your peaceful friends deceived you and will overpower you. They will bring your feet to rest in slippery places; they turned away from you.
units.Jeremiah 45:23: They will bring your wives and children out to the Chaldeans. You certainly will not be saved, for Babylon’s king will seize you, and this city will be burned.
units.Jeremiah 45:24: The king said to him, Let no one learn anything of these words, and you certainly will not die.
units.Jeremiah 45:25: If the rulers hear that I spoke to you, come to you, and say, Tell us what the king said to you. Hide nothing from us and we certainly will not kill you. What did the king say to you?
units.Jeremiah 45:26: tell them, I am casting my appeal for mercy before the king’s eyes, not to send me back to Jonathan’s house to die there.
units.Jeremiah 45:27: All the rulers came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He reported everything the king had instructed him, and they fell silent, because the Lord’s word had not been heard.
units.Jeremiah 45:28: Jeremiah remained in the prison court until the time Jerusalem was captured.
units.Jeremiah 46:1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his whole force arrived against Jerusalem and besieged it.
units.Jeremiah 46:2: In Zedekiah’s eleventh year, on the ninth day of the fourth month, the city was breached.
units.Jeremiah 46:3: All Babylon’s king’s commanders entered and sat at the Middle Gate: Nargalasar, Samagoth, Nabousachar, Nabousaris, Nagargasnaser Rabamag, and the remaining commanders of Babylon’s king.
units.Jeremiah 46:14: They sent and took Jeremiah from the prison court and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan. They brought him out, and he lived among the people.
units.Jeremiah 46:15: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah in the prison court:
units.Jeremiah 46:16: Go and tell Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: I am bringing My words upon this city for calamity, not good.
units.Jeremiah 46:17: I will save you that day and certainly will not hand you over to the men you fear.
units.Jeremiah 46:18: I will certainly save you. You certainly will not fall by the sword; your life will be your gain because you trusted in Me, says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 47:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah afterward, after Nebuzaradan, the chief guard from Daman, sent him away, when he took him in handcuffs among Judah’s exiles who were being led to Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 47:2: The chief guard took him and said to him, The Lord your God spoke these calamities against this place.
units.Jeremiah 47:3: And the Lord acted, because you sinned against Him and did not obey His voice.
units.Jeremiah 47:4: Behold, I have released you from the handcuffs on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you.
units.Jeremiah 47:5: But if not, go off and return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom Babylon’s king appointed in Judah’s land, and live with him among the people in Judah’s land. Go wherever it seems good in your eyes to go. The chief guard gave him gifts and sent him away.
units.Jeremiah 47:6: He came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and lived among the people left in the land.
units.Jeremiah 47:7: All the commanders of the force in the countryside, they and their men, heard that Babylon’s king had appointed Gedaliah in the land and had entrusted to him men and their wives whom he had not deported to Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 47:8: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ophe the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, they and their men.
units.Jeremiah 47:9: Gedaliah swore to them and their men, saying, Do not be afraid of the Chaldeans’ servants. Live in the land and work for Babylon’s king, and it will be better for you.
units.Jeremiah 47:10: Behold, I am staying before you at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come against you. Gather wine and summer fruit, gather oil, put them in your containers, and live in the cities you have taken over.
units.Jeremiah 47:11: All the Judeans in Moab’s land, among Ammon’s people, in Idumea, and in all the land heard that Babylon’s king had left a remnant for Judah and appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over them.
units.Jeremiah 47:12: They came to Gedaliah in Judah’s land at Mizpah and gathered a very great amount of wine and summer fruit, and oil.
units.Jeremiah 47:13: Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the force in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
units.Jeremiah 47:14: They said to him, Do you really know that Belisa king of Ammon’s people has sent Ishmael to you to take your life? But Gedaliah did not believe them.
units.Jeremiah 47:15: Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Let me go and strike down Ishmael, and let no one know, lest he take your life and all Judah gathered to you be scattered, and Judah’s survivors perish.
units.Jeremiah 47:16: Gedaliah said to Johanan, Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsehoods about Ishmael.
units.Jeremiah 48:1: In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elasa, of the king’s family, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They ate bread together there.
units.Jeremiah 48:2: Ishmael and the ten men with him rose and struck Gedaliah, whom Babylon’s king had appointed over the land,
units.Jeremiah 48:3: and all the Judeans with him at Mizpah, and all the Chaldeans found there.
units.Jeremiah 48:4: On the second day after he struck Gedaliah, when no one knew,
units.Jeremiah 48:5: eighty men came from Shechem, Salem, and Samaria, with shaved beards and torn clothes, beating themselves, carrying grain offerings and frankincense to bring to the Lord’s house.
units.Jeremiah 48:6: Ishmael went out to meet them. They were walking and weeping, and he said to them, Come in to Gedaliah.
units.Jeremiah 48:7: When they entered the middle of the city, he slaughtered them into the cistern.
units.Jeremiah 48:8: Ten men found there said to Ishmael, Do not kill us, for we have stores in the countryside: wheat, barley, honey, and oil. He passed them by and did not kill them among their brothers.
units.Jeremiah 48:9: The cistern into which Ishmael threw all those he had struck down is a large cistern that King Asa made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with the slain.
units.Jeremiah 48:10: Ishmael turned back all the people left at Mizpah and the king’s daughters whom the chief guard had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and he went away to the far side of Ammon’s people.
units.Jeremiah 48:11: Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the force with him heard of all the evils Ishmael had done.
units.Jeremiah 48:12: They led their entire army and went away to fight him. They found him beside abundant water at Gibeon.
units.Jeremiah 48:13: When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan and the commanders of the force with him,
units.Jeremiah 48:15: Ishmael escaped with eight men and went away to Ammon’s people.
units.Jeremiah 48:16: Johanan and all the commanders of the force with him took all the people left whom he had brought back from Ishmael: men mighty in war, the women, the rest, and the eunuchs whom he brought back from Gibeon.
units.Jeremiah 48:17: They went away and stayed at Gaberoth-chamaam near Bethlehem, intending to go into Egypt,
units.Jeremiah 48:18: away from the Chaldeans, for they feared them because Ishmael had struck Gedaliah, whom Babylon’s king had appointed in the land.
units.Jeremiah 49:1: All the commanders of the force, Johanan, Azariah son of Maaseiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, approached
units.Jeremiah 49:2: Jeremiah the prophet and said to him, Please let our appeal for mercy come before you. Pray to the Lord your God for these survivors, for few of us remain out of many, as your eyes see.
units.Jeremiah 49:3: Let the Lord your God tell us the way we should go and the matter we should carry out.
units.Jeremiah 49:4: Jeremiah said to them, I have heard. I will pray to the Lord our God as you have said. Whatever word the Lord answers, I will tell you; I certainly will not hide a word from you.
units.Jeremiah 49:5: They said to Jeremiah, May the Lord be a righteous and faithful witness among us if we do not act according to every word with which the Lord sends you to us.
units.Jeremiah 49:6: Whether good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be better for us, because we will obey the voice of the Lord our God.
units.Jeremiah 49:7: After ten days, the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah.
units.Jeremiah 49:8: He called Johanan, the commanders of the force, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
units.Jeremiah 49:9: He said to them, Thus said the Lord:
units.Jeremiah 49:10: If you remain in this land, I will build you up and certainly not tear you down; I will plant you and certainly not pluck you up. For I have rested from the calamities I brought upon you.
units.Jeremiah 49:11: Do not fear Babylon’s king, whom you fear. Do not fear, says the Lord, for I am with you to rescue you and save you from his hand.
units.Jeremiah 49:12: I will grant you mercy, have mercy on you, and return you to your land.
units.Jeremiah 49:13: But if you say, We certainly will not remain in this land, so as not to obey the Lord’s voice,
units.Jeremiah 49:14: because we will enter Egypt’s land, certainly not see war or hear the trumpet’s sound or hunger for bread, and there we will live—
units.Jeremiah 49:15: therefore hear the Lord’s word. Thus said the Lord: If you set your faces toward Egypt and go in to live there,
units.Jeremiah 49:16: the sword you fear will find you in Egypt’s land, and the famine you are concerned about will catch up with you from behind in Egypt, and there you will die.
units.Jeremiah 49:17: All the people and all the foreigners who set their faces toward Egypt’s land to live there will perish by sword and famine. None of them will be saved from the calamities I am bringing upon them.
units.Jeremiah 49:18: For thus said the Lord: As My wrath dripped upon Jerusalem’s inhabitants, so My wrath will drip upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become an untrodden place, subject to others, a curse, and a reproach, and you certainly will never see this place again.
units.Jeremiah 49:19: These are the things the Lord spoke concerning you, Judah’s survivors: Do not enter Egypt. And now know for certain
units.Jeremiah 49:20: that you acted wickedly in your souls when you sent me, saying, Pray for us to the Lord, and we will do everything the Lord tells you.
units.Jeremiah 49:21: And you did not obey the Lord’s voice, with which He sent me to you.
units.Jeremiah 49:22: And now you will perish by sword and famine in the place where you want to go and live.
units.Jeremiah 50:1: When Jeremiah stopped speaking to the people all the Lord’s words, with which the Lord had sent him to them—all these words—
units.Jeremiah 50:2: Azariah son of Maaseiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the men who spoke said to Jeremiah, You are lying! The Lord did not send you to us to say, Do not enter Egypt to live there.
units.Jeremiah 50:3: Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is setting you against us, so that you will hand us over to the Chaldeans, to put us to death and have us deported to Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 50:4: Johanan, all the commanders of the force, and all the people did not obey the Lord’s voice by remaining in Judah’s land.
units.Jeremiah 50:5: Johanan and all the commanders of the force took all Judah’s survivors who had returned to live in the land:
units.Jeremiah 50:6: the mighty men, the women, the little children, the king’s daughters, the people Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
units.Jeremiah 50:7: They entered Egypt, for they had not obeyed the Lord’s voice. They entered Taphnas.
units.Jeremiah 50:8: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah at Taphnas:
units.Jeremiah 50:9: Take large stones for yourself and hide them in the forecourt at the gate of Pharaoh’s house at Taphnas, before the eyes of Judah’s men.
units.Jeremiah 50:10: Say, Thus said the Lord: I am sending and will bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will place his throne above these stones that you hid and raise his weapons over them.
units.Jeremiah 50:11: He will enter and strike Egypt’s land: those for death, to death; those for deportation, to deportation; and those for the sword, to the sword.
units.Jeremiah 50:12: He will kindle fire in the houses of their gods, burn the houses, and deport the gods. He will delouse Egypt’s land as a shepherd delouses his garment, and he will go out in peace.
units.Jeremiah 50:13: He will shatter the pillars of the City of the Sun, those in On, and burn their houses with fire.
units.Jeremiah 51:1: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in Egypt’s land and those staying at Migdol, Taphnas, and in Pathoures’s land:
units.Jeremiah 51:2: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: You have seen all the calamities I brought upon Jerusalem and Judah’s cities. Behold, they are deserted of inhabitants,
units.Jeremiah 51:3: because of the wickedness they committed to embitter Me, going to burn incense to other gods whom you did not know.
units.Jeremiah 51:4: I sent you My servants the prophets at dawn, and I sent them saying, Do not commit this act of defilement that I hate.
units.Jeremiah 51:5: But they did not listen to Me or incline their ear to turn from their evils and stop burning incense to other gods.
units.Jeremiah 51:6: My anger and wrath dripped out and blazed in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, and they became a desolation and an untrodden place, as on this day.
units.Jeremiah 51:7: Now thus said the Lord Almighty: Why are you doing great evils against yourselves, cutting off from yourselves man and woman, little child and nursing infant from Judah, so that none of you remains,
units.Jeremiah 51:8: embittering Me with the work of your hands by burning incense to other gods in Egypt’s land, which you entered to live there, so that you are cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the earth’s nations?
units.Jeremiah 51:9: Have you forgotten your fathers’ evils, the evils of Judah’s kings, your rulers’ evils, and your wives’ evils, which they committed in Judah’s land and outside Jerusalem?
units.Jeremiah 51:10: They have not stopped to this day and have not held fast to My ordinances, which I set before their fathers.
units.Jeremiah 51:11: Therefore thus said the Lord: I am setting My face
units.Jeremiah 51:12: to destroy all the survivors in Egypt, and they will fall. By sword and famine they will perish, from the least to the greatest, and become a reproach, a destruction, and a curse.
units.Jeremiah 51:13: I will visit those staying in Egypt’s land as I visited Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and death.
units.Jeremiah 51:14: None of Judah’s remainder residing in Egypt’s land will be saved to return to Judah’s land, where they hope in their souls to return. They certainly will not return except those rescued.
units.Jeremiah 51:15: All the men who knew that their wives burned incense to other gods, all the women, a great assembly, and all the people staying in Egypt’s land at Pathoures answered Jeremiah:
units.Jeremiah 51:16: As for the word you spoke to us in the Lord’s name, we will not listen to you.
units.Jeremiah 51:17: We will certainly do everything that will come from our mouths: burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem. We were filled with bread, were well off, and saw no calamities.
units.Jeremiah 51:18: But when we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven, we were all diminished and perished by sword and famine.
units.Jeremiah 51:19: And when we burn incense to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands?
units.Jeremiah 51:20: Jeremiah said to all the people—to the mighty men, the women, and all the people who had answered him:
units.Jeremiah 51:21: Was it not the incense you burned in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem—you, your fathers, your kings, your rulers, and the people of the land—that the Lord remembered, and did it not come into His heart?
units.Jeremiah 51:22: The Lord could no longer bear the wickedness of your actions and the abominations you had committed. Your land became a desolation, an untrodden place, and a curse, as on this day,
units.Jeremiah 51:23: because you burned incense, sinned against the Lord, did not obey the Lord’s voice, and did not walk in His ordinances, law, and testimonies. These calamities have seized you.
units.Jeremiah 51:24: Jeremiah said to the people and the women, Hear the Lord’s word:
units.Jeremiah 51:25: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: You women spoke with your mouths and fulfilled it with your hands, saying, We will certainly carry out our pledges that we pledged, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her. You firmly persisted in your pledges and indeed carried them out.
units.Jeremiah 51:26: Therefore hear the Lord’s word, all Judah staying in Egypt’s land: I have sworn by My great name, said the Lord, that My name will no longer be in any Judean’s mouth to say, As the Lord, the Lord, lives, throughout Egypt’s land.
units.Jeremiah 51:27: For I am watching over them to harm them, not do them good. All Judah living in Egypt’s land will perish by sword and famine until they perish.
units.Jeremiah 51:28: Those saved from the sword will return to Judah’s land, few in number. Judah’s survivors who settled in Egypt’s land to live there will know whose word will endure.
units.Jeremiah 51:29: This will be the sign for you that I will visit you for evils:
units.Jeremiah 51:30: Thus said the Lord: I am handing Ouaphre king of Egypt over to his enemy and those seeking his life, as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.
units.Jeremiah 51:31: The word Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in the scroll from Jeremiah’s mouth, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
units.Jeremiah 51:32: Thus said the Lord concerning you, Baruch:
units.Jeremiah 51:33: For you said, Woe to me, woe to me! The Lord has added toil to my pain. I lay down amid groanings and found no rest.
units.Jeremiah 51:34: Tell him, Thus said the Lord: Those I have built up I am tearing down, and those I have planted I am plucking up.
units.Jeremiah 51:35: Are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them, for I am bringing calamities upon all flesh, says the Lord. I will give your life as gain wherever you walk.
units.Jeremiah 52:1: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Amitaal daughter of Jeremiah, from Lobena.
units.Jeremiah 52:4: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his force came against Jerusalem. They enclosed her with a palisade and built around her with squared stones.
units.Jeremiah 52:5: The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
units.Jeremiah 52:6: On the ninth of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there were no loaves for the people of the land.
units.Jeremiah 52:7: The city was breached, and all the warriors went out at night by the gate between the wall and the outer wall beside the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city. They went by the road to Arabah,
units.Jeremiah 52:8: and the Chaldean force pursued the king and overtook him beyond Jericho. All his servants scattered away from him.
units.Jeremiah 52:9: They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he spoke to him in judgment.
units.Jeremiah 52:10: The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he slaughtered all Judah’s rulers at Deblatha.
units.Jeremiah 52:11: He blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him in fetters. The king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in a mill house until the day he died.
units.Jeremiah 52:12: In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuzaradan, the chief guard who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
units.Jeremiah 52:13: He burned the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all the city’s houses; every great house he burned with fire.
units.Jeremiah 52:14: The Chaldean force with the chief guard pulled down the whole wall of Jerusalem all around.
units.Jeremiah 52:16: The chief guard left the remaining people as vinedressers and farmers.
units.Jeremiah 52:17: The Chaldeans shattered the bronze pillars in the Lord’s house, the bases, and the bronze Sea in the Lord’s house. They took their bronze and carried it to Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 52:18: And the rim, the bowls, the meat forks, and all the bronze utensils with which they performed service,
units.Jeremiah 52:19: and the saphphoth, the masmaroth, the pouring vessels, the lampstands, the incense bowls, and the ladles—those of gold, gold, and those of silver, silver—the chief guard took.
units.Jeremiah 52:20: The two pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze calves beneath the Sea, which King Solomon made for the Lord’s house—their bronze was beyond weighing.
units.Jeremiah 52:21: As for the pillars, one pillar was thirty-five cubits high, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it. Its thickness was four fingerbreadths all around,
units.Jeremiah 52:22: and a bronze cornice was on them. The projection of one cornice was five cubits in length, and a net and pomegranates surrounded the cornice, all of bronze. The second pillar had the same: eight pomegranates per cubit over the twelve cubits.
units.Jeremiah 52:23: There were ninety-six pomegranates on one side; all the pomegranates around the net numbered one hundred.
units.Jeremiah 52:24: The chief guard took the first priest, the second priest, and the three men guarding the road,
units.Jeremiah 52:25: and one eunuch who supervised the warriors, seven prominent men in the king’s presence who were found in the city, the scribe of the forces who kept records for the people of the land, and sixty people from the people of the land found inside the city.
units.Jeremiah 52:26: Nebuzaradan, the chief guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha,
units.Jeremiah 52:27: and the king of Babylon struck them at Deblatha in Aimath’s land.
units.Jeremiah 52:31: In the thirty-seventh year after Ioakim king of Judah had been deported, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth of the month, Oulaimaradach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, took up the head of Ioakim king of Judah and brought him out of the house where he was guarded.
units.Jeremiah 52:32: He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings with him in Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 52:33: He changed his prison robe, and he ate bread continually before him all the days he lived.
units.Jeremiah 52:34: His allowance was given to him continually by the king of Babylon, from day to day until the day he died.
